newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Heating oil pours into U.S. Northeast.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Heating oil pours into U.S. Northeast.

text.p: Heating oil poured into the U.S. Northeast last week, heartwarming news for consumers that was expected to give futures traders a case of heartburn.
Heating oil supplies in the (PADD I) East Coast rose 1.36 million barrels last week, just in time for below-normal temperatures due in Northeast states over the next 10 days.
The forecast of cooler weather and perceptions of lean heating oil stocks had fueled a rise in heating oil futures, which ended the floor session up 1.83 cents at 73.68 cents a gallon.

"That should take a little bit of the wind out of the bullish sails," ING Futures and Options Inc energy analyst Tom Bentz. "If heat goes down tomorrow, it should pull the crude and gas down with it."

While heating oil supplies were building in the East Coast, refiners along the PADD III Gulf Coast region reported a draw of 1.69 million barrels for the week ended November 15, the Washington, D.C.-based trade group said.
The Gulf Coast draw was seen as evidence of increased shipments to the Northeast, where distillate stocks overall remained 15.05 million barrels below the same week last year.
U.S. refiners, under pressure to step up distillate output, were operating at 92.9 percent of capacity, up 2.2 percentage points from the prior week, API said.

Refiners in the PADD II Midwest market were running at a blistering 98.7 percent of capacity, API said. The 8.7 percentage point jump was tied to the restart of a fluid catalytic cracker at Clark Refining and Marketing Co's 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery.
Clark doubled gasoline output at the Chicago-area refinery to two million gallons per day after a state court dismissed a lawsuit seeking to idle the refinery over safety concerns.

Nationwide, gasoline supplies were drawn down 535,000 barrels for the week, and remained 4.72 million barrels below the same week last year, API said. The draw was fueled by a 1.85 million barrel drop in East Coast gasoline stocks.

The API for the second straight week revised its crude oil estimates, pegging crude inventories nationwide at 302.31 million barrels. The net 3.5 million barrel draw left crude stocks 9.9 million barrels below the same week last year.

Midwest refiners reported a 2.44 million barrel draw for the week. Inventories also fell 3.2 million barrels in the PADD V West Coast region, where refiners said stocks were 15.3 million barrels below the same week last year.

Crude imports fell to an average 6.92 million barrels per day, down a net 1.2 million barrels per day on the week. Imports of refined products eased to an average 1.78 million barrels per day, off a net 235,000 barrels per day, API said.
